items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 4.6.3 at source lines 571-573: f is an equivalence if and only if it is surjective and an embedding. The author's proof (source lines 574-586) separates the two directions cleanly and the converse is a real argument: surjectivity gives only a truncated inhabitant of the fiber, so after that step the work is to show the fiber is a mere proposition (lines 578-581), and for two fiber elements (x,p) and (y,q) the embedding property produces r : x = y with ap f (r) = p `ct` opp q (lines 582-583), which must then be rearranged by the characterisation of paths in sigma types into the transport statement trans r p = q before r and it can be exhibited as a path in the fiber (lines 584-585). The statement gives no hint that the embedding property is used to produce a path in the source that is then transported.
